Key Insights — Executive Summary

  1. Bangladesh's registered pesticide inventory comprises 5,452 products. Of these, 4,140 (75.9%) are mapped to 55 distinct MoA codes across IRAC, FRAC, and HRAC schemes; 1,312 (24.1%) have no MoA code assigned and require PTAC attention for register reconciliation.
  2. Insecticides dominate the inventory with 2,396 IRAC-classified products (~43.9% of total), reflecting strong reliance on nerve-acting compounds such as IRAC 1B (organophosphates) and IRAC 3A (pyrethroids).
  3. The top 5 MoA codes (IRAC 1B (545), IRAC 4A (489), IRAC 3A (420), IRAC 6 (394), FRAC 3 (274)) collectively account for 2,122 products — concentrated exposure that elevates resistance-selection pressure.
  4. 979 fungicide products are mapped to FRAC groups; FRAC M3 (dithiocarbamate multi-site protectants) and FRAC 3 (DMI azoles) are the most numerous, supporting rotation strategies when paired with single-site MoAs.
  5. 765 herbicide products are mapped to HRAC groups; HRAC B (ALS inhibitors) is the most represented, a class with globally documented resistance risk that warrants stewardship in rice and wheat systems.
  6. Resistance rotation guidance: PTAC encourages alternating applications across different MoA Group Numbers (e.g. IRAC Group 1 → 4 → 6 → 28) and avoiding consecutive applications of any single MoA within a cropping cycle.
  7. The Product MoA Mapping section contains the complete official record (5,452 rows) for cross-checking registration numbers against MoA assignments prior to PTAC review.

Notes & Definitions

MoAMode of Action — the biochemical mechanism by which a pesticide acts on the target pest.
IRACInsecticide Resistance Action Committee — classifies insecticides and miticides by MoA group.
FRACFungicide Resistance Action Committee — classifies fungicides by MoA group.
HRACHerbicide Resistance Action Committee — classifies herbicides by MoA group.
IRMInsecticide / Pesticide Resistance Management — practices to delay resistance evolution, including MoA rotation.
RotationSequential use of products from different MoA Group Numbers to disrupt resistance selection.
Multi-siteMoA acting on multiple biochemical targets simultaneously (e.g. mancozeb, chlorothalonil); low resistance risk.
Single-siteMoA acting on a single specific target; higher resistance risk; rotation essential.
Disclaimer: This MoA mapping is prepared for the Pesticide Technical Appraisal Committee (PTAC) based on the registered pesticide database. MoA classifications follow current IRAC, FRAC, and HRAC reference lists. Verify against the latest authority-published reference before regulatory action.
